definitions.explanation: Sake produced by a local brewery, typically associated with a particular region and reflecting its water, rice, and brewing traditions. Valued for regional character and artisanal quality.

examples.japanese: この{地酒|じざけ}はおいしい。
{旅先|たびさき}で{地酒|じざけ}を{飲|の}むのが{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: I look forward to drinking local sake when I travel.

examples.japanese: この{居酒屋|いざかや}は{全国|ぜんこく}の{地酒|じざけ}を{豊富|ほうふ}に{取|と}り{揃|そろ}えている。
examples.english: This izakaya has an extensive selection of local sake from across the country.

notes: The prefix {地|じ}～ indicates something local or regional: {地元|じもと} (local area), {地ビール|じびーる} (craft/local beer). Japanese sake culture places great value on regional varieties, and {地酒|じざけ} is a common draw for tourists visiting rural areas. Common collocations: {地酒|じざけ}を{味|あじ}わう (to savor local sake), {地酒|じざけ}の{飲|の}み{比|くら}べ (local sake tasting comparison). Related: {日本酒|にほんしゅ} (Japanese sake — general term), {銘酒|めいしゅ} (fine/renowned sake).
